title: Chapter 5: 25 Minutes and 14 Seconds!
html:
“Skills and talents? So Nightmare Mission rewards are different—they benefit me directly!”

Chen Ge committed that detail to memory, his anticipation growing. He had caught a glimpse of another world—a place of terror, darkness, and danger. Perhaps that was where his parents had gone, but with his current abilities, he could barely protect himself, much less search for them. Fortunately, as long as he had the black phone, there was still hope.

“That’s still a long way off. For now, I need to stabilize the Haunted House and survive this financial crisis.” He pulled out his phone. “That was close. Something could have gone seriously wrong. Nightmare Missions clearly aren’t easy. Then again, there’s no reason to handle everything alone. In the information age, help is right at my fingertips.”

He logged onto several popular supernatural forums and uploaded the original video.

Within seconds, the video had acquired a title: ‘Who Is That in the Mirror?’

Views and shares began climbing rapidly. Perhaps people were tired of the endless stream of gossip and ordinary news and wanted something different. The video’s popularity shot upward; every time Chen Ge refreshed the page, at least ten new comments appeared.

“25:14. You all can thank me later.”

“Has the uploader lost his mind? Who would do something like this in the middle of the night?”

“Why did the mirror crack on its own? And what was that thing that hit it near the end?!”

“The cracks were probably caused by sudden temperature changes in the room.”

“No, you’re all wrong. In Daoism, mirrors are objects saturated with yin energy. I say we change the title from ‘Who Is That in the Mirror?’ to ‘The Ghost in the Mirror!’”

“Jesus Christ, who would dare do something this crazy in the middle of the night?! I have to respect the uploader’s nerve.”

“This video has definitely been edited. If it hasn’t, remember my username—I’ll do a handstand and eat shit!”

“Am I the only one who noticed this? The uploader’s profile says he owns a Haunted House in Western Jiujiang. Don’t get so worked up; this is obviously just a staged advertisement.”

Chen Ge’s inbox instantly filled with private messages. Some contained questions, others accusations, but he ignored them all. He knew the video was real and did not feel he owed anyone an explanation. People who understood what they were seeing would recognize its authenticity; as for those determined to undermine him, why waste time arguing?

Watching the video’s meteoric rise in popularity, Chen Ge suddenly realized he had stumbled onto a good opportunity. He clipped the final fourteen seconds from the original recording and uploaded the segment to the country’s largest video-sharing app.

Among endless clips of food, dancing, and singing, his horror video was certainly one of a kind.

In less than ten seconds, people began falling into his trap. Unlike users on supernatural forums, who actively searched for this sort of material, random viewers were being frightened without warning—and promptly flooded the comments with angry complaints.

Unfortunately for them, conflict and controversy attracted more viewers online than praise ever could. The wave of criticism only drove the view count higher. Scrolling through the comments, Chen Ge could practically feel the anger directed at him, but he merely laughed it off.

To be fair, he understood why people reacted that way. Most were probably lying in bed, wrapped in blankets and scrolling through lighthearted videos before going to sleep. A frightening clip of a man surrounded by candlelight was exactly the opposite of what they had expected.

The “best” part was that the clip lasted only fourteen seconds. Before viewers could even understand what was happening, the scare had already landed: the mirror cracked, and the figure inside seemed to charge out of the glass and straight through the phone screen.

The setup was masterful.

With the comment section this lively, the video probably isn’t losing popularity anytime soon… That means everyone likes it, right?A certain shameless someone asked himself rhetorically. I’ve already gained another hundred followers. If I don’t use this chance to advertise the Haunted House, I’ll be letting all my new followers down!

Chen Ge changed the video title and added the Haunted House’s address to his profile. He even gave it a tagline: A Completely Not Scary Haunted House.

Satisfied with his updated profile, Chen Ge remained beneath the window, scrolling through the flood of messages until he eventually fell asleep.

…

Chen Ge woke to sunlight falling across his face. He stretched his aching body and rose from the corner of the bathroom.

“It’s already 8:30 a.m.?!” He dusted off his clothes, pocketed the doll and the phone, and left the bathroom.

He noticed deep scratch marks along the edges of the wooden bathroom door, as though rodents had been gnawing at it.

“Just what was outside the door last night?” Seeing the marks, Chen Ge was suddenly grateful that he had stayed in front of the mirror instead of going outside to investigate.

“Nightmare Missions can have unforeseen consequences. I need to be more careful in the future.” Since the Haunted House showed no other obvious changes, Chen Ge set the matter aside and prepared for a new day.

New Century Park opened at 9:00 a.m. At 8:45, a slender young woman came hurrying toward him with a backpack.

“Boss!” The girl radiated youthful energy, her features bright in the morning sun.

“Xiao Wan, perfect timing. I just added a new background track to our music library. Listen to it and tell me what you think.” Before Chen Ge could finish, Xu Wan grabbed his hand. Startled, he asked, “What are you doing?!”

“I just saw a huge crowd gathered at the park entrance! They’re all talking about the Haunted House! People actually came here just to visit us!” Xu Wan exclaimed. “Boss, we have a lot of customers waiting!”

“Isn’t that normal? Is this your first day at the park?” Chen Ge pretended not to care. He pulled out his phone and checked the video-sharing app. His follower count had passed five hundred, and the video had entered the platform’s top ten. Unlike most comment sections, which were full of hearts and affectionate messages, his overflowed with complaints, curses, and threats. Some viewers even claimed they were already on their way to confront him in person.

“Uh, this may have gotten slightly out of hand.” Chen Ge coughed awkwardly and pulled Xu Wan into the Haunted House. “We still have fifteen minutes before the park officially opens. Since we’re the only two left holding down the fort, brace yourself for battle!”
